questions.question: Who introduced the E‑R data model?
questions.explanation:
The E‑R data model was introduced by Chen in 1976. (Source Page: [63])  

---

questions.question: Which work is a collection of papers on the E‑R model?
questions.explanation:
Davis et al. [1983] provides a collection of papers on the E‑R model. (Source Page: [63])  

---

questions.question: In the evaluation scenario, why is a quaternary relationship required?

options.A: To allow many‑to‑many connections between students and projects
options.B: To represent the (project, instructor) combination associated with an evaluation
options.C: To simplify the E‑R diagram by omitting attributes

questions.explanation:
A quaternary relationship is needed because a binary relationship between student and evaluation would not permit representation of the (project, instructor) combination to which an evaluation corresponds. (Source Page: [43])

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT listed as a commercial tool for E‑R diagramming?
questions.explanation:
The context lists IBM Rational Rose, Microsoft Visio, CA’s ERwin, Poseidon for UML, and SmartDraw, but does not mention Oracle SQL Developer Data Modeler. (Source Page: [63])  

---

questions.question: Which publication provides a detailed textbook coverage of research in E‑R modeling?
questions.explanation:
Thalheim [2000] is cited as providing a detailed textbook coverage of research in E‑R modeling. (Source Page: [63])

questions.question: What does the IDEF1X standard define?

options.A: A methodology for relational database normalization
options.C: A query language for hierarchical databases

questions.explanation:
The Integration Definition for Information Modeling (IDEF1X) standard defines standards for E‑R diagrams. (Source Page: [63])  

---

questions.question: Which statement best describes a weak entity set?

options.A: It has its own primary key independent of any other entity.
options.C: It depends on a strong entity for its identification.
options.D: It is always represented with a double rectangle in an E‑R diagram.

questions.explanation:
A weak entity set does not have a primary key of its own and relies on a strong (owner) entity for identification. (Source Page: [61])  

---

questions.question: Which authors are noted for providing basic textbook discussions of E‑R modeling?
questions.explanation:
Batini et al. [1992] (along with Elmasri and Navathe) are mentioned as offering basic textbook discussions. (Source Page: [63])

questions.question: Practice Exercise 7.16 asks students to construct what?

options.A: Entity‑relationship diagrams for a new university database
options.B: Appropriate relation schemas for each of the E‑R diagrams in Exercises 7.1‑7.3
options.C: A UML class diagram for a library system
options.D: A SQL query to retrieve all weak entities

questions.explanation:
Exercise 7.16 requests the construction of appropriate relation schemas for each of the E‑R diagrams in Practice Exercises 7.1 to 7.3. (Source Page: [61])  

---

questions.question: In what year did Teorey et al. present a logical design methodology using the extended E‑R model?
questions.explanation: Teorey et al. [1986] presented a logical design methodology for relational databases using the extended E‑R model. (Source Page: [63])
